(PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ASHOK S. KINAGI)

These appeals are filed by the appellants/petitioners being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded vide judgments and awards dated 01.02.2021 passed in MVC Nos.198 of 2018 and 199 of 2018 by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-XII, Ballari ('Tribunal' for short).
2. Brief facts leading rise to the filing of these appeals are as follows:
2.1.

On 11.12.2017, the petitioner in MVC No.198 of 2018, and the minor petitioner in MVC No.199 of 2018 (daughter of the petitioner in MVC No.198 of 2018) were sitting near the house of Chinna Lingappa at Yerrakondapura Village.

At that time, the driver of the Mahindra Bolero bearing Reg.No.AP-02/TA-0776 drove the same in rash and negligent manner, and dashed against the petitioners, due to which, the petitioners have sustained grievous injuries.

The petitioners filed separate NC:
2026:KHC-D:3589 HC-KAR claim petitions in MVC Nos.198 of 2018 and 199 of 2018 under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1998 seeking compensations on account of the injuries sustained by them in the road traffic accident.
Accordingly, prays to allow the claim petitions.
2.2. The Tribunal tried both the claim petitions separately.
2.3. Respondent Nos.1 to 3 appeared before the Tribunal through their respective counsels, however, respondent No.1-Driver and respondent No.2-Owner did not file the statement of objections.

2.4. Respondent No.3-Insurance Company filed separate statements of objections in the respective claim petitions denying the averments made in the claim petitions, and contending that, driver of the offending vehicle did not posses a valid and effective driving licence as of the date of accident.
Hence, prays to dismiss the claim petitions.
The Tribunal, based on the pleadings of the parties, framed the relevant issues in both the petitions respectively.
2.6. The petitioner in MVC No. 198 of 2018 examined herself as PW1, examined the Doctor as PW2 and marked 8 documents as Exs.P1 to P8 and 1 photograph as MO1.
The father of the petitioner in MVC No. 199 of 2018 was examined as PW1, examined the doctor as PW2 and marked 9 documents as Exs.P1 to P9 and 1 photograph as MO1.
In both the petitions, no evidence was led by the respondents.

2.7. The Tribunal, after assessing the verbal and documentary evidence, allowed the claim petitions in part with costs vide judgments dated 01.02.2021 and awarded a compensation of 4,16,800/-
with interest at the rate of 7% per annum to the petitioner in MVC No.198 of 2018; 3,87,000/- with interest at the rate of 7% per annum to the minor petitioner in MVC No.199 of 2018, from the date NC: 2026:KHC-D:3589 HC-KAR of petition till the entire amount is deposited, and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount along with the interest.

4 3.
The petitioners in both the claim petitions, being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal filed these appeals.
MFA No. 101072 of 2021 is arising out of MVC No. 198 of 2018 and MFA No. 101075 of 2021 is arising out of MVC No. 199 of 2018.

4. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the petitioners and also learned counsel for the Insurance Company.
5.
Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that, the compensations awarded by the Tribunal are on the lower side.

He further submits that, the petitioner in MVC No. 198 of 2018 examined the Doctor as PW2, who has opined that the petitioner has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 38% to the whole body, wherein NC: 2026:KHC-D:3589 HC-KAR the Tribunal has taken the disability at 13%, which is on the lower side.
He further submits that, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the other heads is also on the lower side.

He submits that, the minor petitioner (through her father) in MVC No. 199 of 2018, examined the doctor as PW2, who has opined that the petitioner has suffered a permanent disability to the extent of 35% to the particular limb, wherein the Tribunal has assessed the disability at 12%, and the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the other heads is also on the lower side.
Hence, on these grounds, he prays to allow the appeals.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that, the award of compensations and assessment of disabilities by the Tribunal are just and proper and do not call for any interference at the hands of this Court.

Hence, on this ground, he prays to dismiss the appeals.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3589 HC-KAR 7.
Perused the records and considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties.
8. The point that would arise for consideration is regarding the quantum of compensation in both the petitions.
9. Admittedly, the petitioners met with an accident, and sustained grievous injuries.
The petitioners have produced a charge sheet at Ex.P4, which discloses that the accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The Tribunal was justified in recording a finding that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Reg. Quantum of compensation in MFA No.101072 of 2021 (MVC No.198 of 2018):
10.
It is the case of the petitioner that she was working as a Coolie and earning 500/- per day.
Because of the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident, the - 10 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:3589 HC-KAR petitioner is unable to work as she used to work previously before the accident.
The petitioner has lost earning capacity.

sentences.text: Although the petitioner has contended that she was working as a Coolie and getting 500/- per month, to substantiate her contention, the petitioner has not produced any income proof.
This Court reassesses the notional income at 10,250/- as the accident is of the year 2017 as per the schedule used by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

The petitioner, to prove the disability, examined the Doctor as PW2 who has deposed that, he has examined the petitioner and issued a disability certificate marked as Ex.P8 and he has opined the petitioner has suffered a permanent disability to the extent of 38% to the whole body, wherein the Tribunal has assessed the disability at 13%, which is on the lower side.
This Court reassesses the disability at 15%.

Considering - 11 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:3589 HC-KAR the entire evidence on record, this Court reassesses the compensation under the following heads:

awarded by the Tribunal.
Thus, the petitioner is entitled to an enhanced compensation of 1,30,250/-.

sentences.text: Quantum of compensation in MFA No.101075 of 2021 (MVC No.199 of 2018):

11. The father of the petitioner was examined as PW1 and Doctor was examined as PW2, who deposed that, he has examined the minor petitioner clinically and radiologically and he opined that the petitioner has suffered a disability to the extent of 35% to the particular limb, wherein the Tribunal has assessed the same 12% to the whole body, which is just and proper.
Considering the entire evidence on record, the Tribunal has granted a compensation of 3,87,000/- which is on the lower side.
The petitioner is entitled to a global compensation of 4,00,000/- including the amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
12. For the foregoing discussion, the point is answered accordingly.

13. In view of the above discussion, I proceed to pass the following:
- 13 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:3589 HC-KAR ORDER i.

The appeals are allowed in part; ii. The impugned judgments and awards are hereby modified;
iii.
The petitioner in MVC No. 198 of 2018 is entitled to a total compensation of 5,47,050/- as against 4,16,800/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Thus, the petitioner is entitled to an enhanced compensation of 1,30,250/-;

iv. The minor petitioner in MVC No. 199 of 2018 is entitled to a global compensation of 4,00,000/- including the amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal; v. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation amounts within 8 weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment in both the petitions; vi. Pending IA(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
